alignments.note: Prepositional predicate carries the supplied copula (rule 49), discontinuous around *not*.
Supplied *The* on the construct, no article morpheme being present in this chain (rule 29).

Corrected: the participle keeps its own English together with the copula the predicate licenses (rule 20), but not the *the*, which the article morpheme on the rectum takes.

Corrected from unrepresented: yôṣēr ha-kōl is a construct chain whose rectum carries the article while the ASV renders it anarthrously (*of all things*) and writes its single *the* at the phrase's left edge; the present article takes that *the* before a supplied one does (rules 29, 47).
*all things* renders kōl with the *of* of the construct relation; head on the lexeme-bearing word (rules 19, 31).
The explicit subject pronoun takes only *he* (rule 20).
The italic *Israel* has no counterpart in the Hebrew of this verse.
Predicate noun takes the supplied copula (rule 20); no article morpheme stands in this chain, so the *the* is supplied on the construct (rule 29).
The *of* belongs to the nomen rectum (rule 19).
In YHWH ṣəbāʾôt šəmô the divine name is the predicate and šēm the subject, so the copula joins this unit (rule 20); it stands after *hosts*, making the unit discontinuous.
The *of* belongs to the nomen rectum (rule 19).

review_notes: The single written *the* of *the former of all things* is moved from the participle to the article on ha-kōl: the chain's rectum carries an article and the ASV renders it anarthrously, which is rule 29's fronting case, and rule 47 states that a present article morpheme takes the English *the* before a supplied one does.
*is his name*: the copula is placed with the fronted predicate YHWH rather than with the subject noun šēm, per rule 20's instruction to read the Hebrew clause rather than English word order.
